Maximal-ratio combining weights each branch by its signal-to-noise ratio, so output SNR is the sum of branch SNRs. Diversity order is the number of independent branches. MIMO uses multiple antennas at both ends. Spatial multiplexing sends up to min(Nt, Nr) parallel streams; spatial diversity improves reliability. For a narrowband channel matrix H, capacity is C = log2 det(I + (ρ/Nt) H H^H) bits/s/Hz, with ρ the total SNR. Example: H = I for 2 × 2 and ρ = 10 gives C = 2 log2(1 + 10/2) = 5.17 bits/s/Hz.

sections.heading: Beamforming and interference
sections.text: Beamforming feeds antenna elements with phase weights so signals add in wanted directions and cancel elsewhere. A steering vector describes the phase across an array. With N elements, coherent combining gives array gain N under fixed total power; if each element keeps its power, power gain is N². Beamforming raises SINR and can reject interference, but it needs channel state information. Interference is measured by SINR = S ÷ (I + N).

sections.heading: Cellular planning
sections.text: Cellular planning controls co-channel interference through frequency reuse, sectorisation and power control. A reuse factor of 1 is common in OFDMA systems, so interference coordination replaces simple frequency planning. Advanced networks add small cells, heterogeneous layers and massive MIMO. Planning uses SINR maps and traffic models, not only coverage. If wanted power is 100 units and interference plus noise is 25 units, SINR = 100 ÷ 25 = 4, or 6.0 dB. Reuse distances and limits depend on the technology and national regulator, so check current official rules.

keyPoints: Rayleigh fading models non-line-of-sight multipath; Rician fading adds a line-of-sight component with K factor.
Delay spread limits coherence bandwidth and Doppler spread limits coherence time.
Maximal-ratio combining sums branch SNRs, and diversity order equals the number of independent branches.
MIMO capacity for a narrowband channel is C = log2 det(I + (ρ/Nt) H H^H) bits/s/Hz.
Beamforming with N elements gives array gain N under fixed total power and needs channel state information.
SINR = S ÷ (I + N), and cellular planning manages co-channel interference through reuse, sectorisation and coordination.

en.title: Optical networks and photonics
en.short: WDM architecture, optical amplifiers, switching, impairments and optical transport design.

sections.heading: WDM architecture
sections.text:
Wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) sends several modulated wavelengths through one fibre. Dense WDM (DWDM) packs them closely on an international frequency grid; check the current ITU-T grid recommendation.

A transponder maps each client signal onto a wavelength. A multiplexer combines wavelengths, a demultiplexer separates them, and an optical add-drop multiplexer (OADM) adds or drops selected wavelengths without converting the others. A reconfigurable OADM (ROADM) allows remote switching. An optical cross-connect (OXC) switches wavelengths between fibres. Networks use point-to-point, ring and mesh topologies.

sections.heading: Amplifiers and noise
sections.text:
An optical amplifier boosts light without converting it to electrical form. The erbium-doped fibre amplifier (EDFA) is common in the C-band; Raman amplifiers use stimulated Raman scattering in the fibre, and semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) are compact but noisier. Gain, noise figure and amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) set the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR). Gain flattening keeps channels equal.

Example: with 4 THz usable bandwidth and 50 GHz spacing, N = 4 THz ÷ 50 GHz = 80 channels. Real counts are lower after guard bands.

sections.heading: Switching and impairments
sections.text:
Switching may be wavelength switching, optical circuit switching or optical packet switching. All-optical packet switching is difficult because light is hard to buffer and headers are hard to process; many networks use optical-electrical-optical (OEO) regeneration at selected nodes.

Impairments include attenuation, chromatic dispersion (CD), polarisation-mode dispersion (PMD), fibre nonlinearities such as self-phase modulation, cross-phase modulation and four-wave mixing, ASE noise and crosstalk. They reduce OSNR and raise bit error rate (BER). Dispersion compensation, power control and regeneration manage them.

sections.heading: Transport design
sections.text:
Design starts with traffic demand and reach. A power budget gives received power: P_rx = P_tx − losses + gains. An OSNR budget checks noise accumulation over spans.

The designer chooses channel spacing, amplifier spacing, fibre type, compensation and regeneration points, then adds margins for ageing and repairs. Protection and restoration keep service after failure. Higher power improves OSNR but worsens nonlinearity, so design is iterative. Check current ITU-T and local regulator requirements.

keyPoints: WDM multiplexes several wavelengths on one fibre; a transponder maps each client signal to a wavelength.
EDFAs, Raman amplifiers and SOAs boost light; ASE and noise figure limit OSNR.
Channel count is approximately amplifier usable bandwidth ÷ channel spacing.
OSNR(dB) = 10 log10(P_signal ÷ P_ASE); higher OSNR lowers BER.
Power budget: P_rx(dBm) = P_tx(dBm) − losses(dB) + gains(dB).
CD, PMD, nonlinearities and crosstalk constrain reach; design trades power against nonlinear penalty.

en.title: Research methods in telecommunications
en.short: Literature review, problem formulation, simulation, measurement, data analysis, ethics and dissertation writing.

sections.heading: Literature and problem
sections.text: A literature review is a critical survey of published work, not a list. It shows what is known, what methods were used and where gaps remain. Read standards, journal papers and conference proceedings, and record sources in a reference manager. Problem formulation turns a gap into a focused research question with scope, variables and success criteria. A good question is answerable with the available time, data and equipment. In telecommunications it may ask whether a proposed scheduling method improves throughput under stated channel conditions.

sections.heading: Simulation and measurement
sections.text: Simulation uses a model, such as a network simulator or a mathematical channel model, to study a system cheaply and repeatably. State the model, assumptions, parameters and random seeds so others can reproduce it. Measurement uses instruments on a real link or prototype. Calibrate instruments, record settings and estimate uncertainty. Simulation should be validated against measurement or theory; agreement within a stated tolerance supports the model. Example: a student simulates throughput as 92 Mbit/s and measures 95 Mbit/s. Percentage error = |92 − 95| ÷ 95 × 100 = 3.16%. That is small only if the stated tolerance allows it.

sections.heading: Data and ethics
sections.text: Data analysis should follow the question. Clean data, state sample size, use plots and summary statistics, and report uncertainty. Do not confuse correlation with cause. Research ethics covers honesty, plagiarism, fabrication, informed consent and data protection. Requirements vary by country and institution; obtain ethics approval before collecting personal data and follow the applicable data protection law. Cite others and keep raw data for checking.

sections.heading: Dissertation writing
sections.text: A dissertation usually has title, abstract, introduction, literature review, method, results, discussion, conclusion and references. Write the method so another student could repeat it. Link each result to the research question. Discuss limitations honestly. Follow your department’s format and citation style; these differ between universities.

keyPoints: A literature review must identify a gap, not just summarise papers.
Formulate a focused, answerable research question with clear scope and success criteria.
Simulation models must state assumptions and be reproducible; validate them against measurement or theory.
Measurement needs calibration, recorded settings and an uncertainty statement.
Percentage error = |simulated − measured| ÷ measured × 100.
Obtain ethics approval where required and write the method so another student could repeat it.
